lore_facts: On Otho, there is a flower said to sing only once, and winged cats gather to drink its nectar.
Othon is also identified here as Shazam.
Bari is dead by this point in the story.

plot_events: Two artificial beings speak; one envies humans for being able to cry and express distress, while the other tells him to be silent and listen to a story or report.
Narration describes a spring evening on Otho where swarms of winged cats move among a rare flower.
Othon, identified in narration as Shazam, rides alone while thinking about his dead son, Bari.
An imperial vessel arrives carrying a long-promised gift.
Othon rides quickly toward the shelter of his fortress because he does not want further disappointment.
Othon shuts himself inside his great hall of weapons.
He orders that the doors not be opened for anyone and refuses visitors.
A servant acknowledges the order as the doors close.

visual_summary: A framed narration page shifts between a machine-filled interior and an outdoor approach to a tall fortress-like structure. Othon/Shazam rides a horse through a landscape filled with fluttering winged creatures toward his stronghold while an imperial ship descends nearby. Inside, attendants and machines receive the arrival. In the final large panel, Othon sits in a chair in his weapons hall holding a limp humanoid figure across his lap, while a servant stands by and heavy doors close with a bright seam of light.
